in_hebrew.name: אילריון
in_hebrew.meaning: אור של אלוהים, שמחה של אל
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם אילריון נגזר מהמילה היוונית 'Ἰλάριος' (Ilarion) שפירושה שמחה או שמח. בקונטקסט הנוצרי, השם מייצג את השמחה והאור שאלוהים מביא לעולם. השם משויך לקדוש נוצרי מהמאה ה-4, אילריון הקדוש, שהיה תלמיד של אנטוניוס הגדול.

in_greek.name: Ιλαρίων
in_greek.meaning: Χαρά του Θεού, Φως του Θεού
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο Ιλαρίων είναι ένα όνομα που προέρχεται από το ελληνικό 'Ἰλάριος' (Ilarion), που σημαίνει χαρά ή ευθυμία. Στην παράδοση της Εκκλησίας, το όνομα συνδέεται με τον Άγιο Ιλαρίωνα, έναν μοναχό και ασκητή του 4ου αιώνα, μαθητή του Αγίου Αντωνίου του Μέγα. Το όνομα αντανακλά τη χαρά και το φως που φέρνει ο Θεός στη ζωή των πιστών.

in_latin.name: Ilarion
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Ilarion derivatur ex voce Graeca 'Ἰλάριος' (Ilarion), quae gaudium seu hilaritatem significat. In traditione Christiana, nomen hoc associatur cum Sancto Ilarione, monacho et asceta saeculi IV, discipulo Sancti Antonii Magni. Nomen ipsum gaudium et lucem reflectit quam Deus in vitam fidelium affert.

in_english.name: Ilarion
in_english.meaning: Joy of God, Light of God
in_english.long_meaning: The name Ilarion originates from the Greek 'Ἰλάριος' (Ilarion), meaning joy or cheerfulness. In Christian tradition, it is associated with Saint Ilarion, a 4th-century monk and ascetic, disciple of Saint Anthony the Great. The name symbolizes the joy and light that God brings into the world, reflecting a profound spiritual significance. Historically, the name has been used in various Christian cultures, signifying a connection to divine happiness and illumination.

Saint Ilarion the Hermit, a 6th-century monk and hermit, is known for his devotion to meditation and prayer in solitude. The name 'Ilarion' holds symbolic value in Christian tradition, representing the connection between the physical and spiritual realms, much like how mountains are seen as metaphysical and spiritual places in various cultures and religions.

historical_references.reference: Ilarion of Dyrrhachium was a prominent Church Father and theologian of the 4th century A.D. He was born in the city of Dyrrhachium (Durres, Albania) and studied under the great theologian Athanasius of Alexandria. Ilarion became a bishop and was known for his strong defense of orthodoxy against various heresies. He is best remembered for his writings, particularly his sermons and letters, which demonstrate his deep understanding of Scripture and theology.

historical_references.reference: Saint Ilarion of Kiev was a monk who lived in the 11th century A.D. in the Russian Orthodox Church. He was born in the town of Chernigov and became a monk at the monastery of the Caves in Kiev. Ilarion is best known for his role in the Christianization of the Rus' people and his missionary work among the Slavic tribes. He is also remembered for his collection of sermons and writings, which were widely disseminated throughout Eastern Europe and played a significant role in the development of Slavic Christianity.
